posts.title: Meeting H.E. Elif Çomoğlu Ülgen, Ambassador of the Republic of Türkiye to Rome
posts.content:
It was a distinct honour to meet H.E. Elif Çomoğlu Ülgen, Ambassador of the Republic of Türkiye to Rome.

Within the framework of my master’s studies in Public and Cultural Diplomacy at the University of Siena, this engagement provided a valuable opportunity to exchange views on contemporary dynamics shaping Türkiye–Italy relations at the societal level.

Our discussion focused particularly on the experience of being a Turkish student in Italy, the recent increase in student mobility from Türkiye to Italian universities, and the evolving role of Turkish student communities across Italy. The conversation highlighted how student migration constitutes not only an educational pathway but also a significant dimension of public diplomacy, people-to-people engagement, and long-term cultural relations.

Such exchanges continue to reinforce my academic focus and professional commitment to the fields of diplomacy, cultural relations, and international education policy.

I am sincerely grateful to H.E. Ambassador Çomoğlu Ülgen for her time, thoughtful reflections, and openness in addressing these themes. The exchange provided a meaningful perspective on the intersection between education, diaspora engagement, and diplomatic representation.

posts.title: Cultural Bridges: Insights from the Yunus Emre Event in Rome
posts.content:
I traveled from Siena to Rome to attend the event “Our Cultural Bridges in Italy,” hosted by the Yunus Emre Enstitüsü. The program offered an enriching space to reflect on the intersections of language, culture, and translation, while engaging with a community committed to fostering intercultural dialogue.

The keynote speaker, translator Nazlı Birgen, shared valuable insights drawn from her many years of professional and personal experience in Italy. Her reflections on bilingual identity, cultural adaptation, and the role of translation in shaping mutual understanding highlighted the importance of cultural mediation in today’s interconnected societies.

As a master’s student in Public and Cultural Diplomacy, I found the event particularly meaningful. The work of the Yunus Emre Institute demonstrated how cultural initiatives can build long-lasting bridges, strengthen diaspora communities, and promote shared values through sustained dialogue. It offered a clear illustration of how cultural diplomacy functions in practice and how it contributes to international engagement.

I extend my sincere appreciation to Beyza Uzun Kutlay, Haluk Soner, and the entire Yunus Emre Institute Rome team for their warm hospitality and excellent organization. I am also grateful to Nazlı Birgen for her thoughtful and inspiring contributions.

The event provided new perspectives and reinforced my motivation to continue contributing to cultural dialogue and international cooperation.

posts.title: Building Bridges: Global Changemakers at Summer Academy 2025
posts.content:
Last week, I participated in the Summer Academy 2025 at Karlshochschule International University in Karlsruhe. The program, Building Bridges: Future Skills for Global Changemakers, was organised by InterCultur gGmbH with the generous support of Stiftung Mercator. The academy brought together young participants from diverse countries and backgrounds for nine days of intensive learning, collaboration, and reflection on global challenges.

The academic program offered a comprehensive set of perspectives on international relations and contemporary global issues. Highlights included lectures on Realism, Constructivism, and Feminism in International Relations by Anthony Teitler, PhD, in-depth discussions on conflict resolution and democratic futures with Marcel Erik Lemmer, and a critical workshop on global security led by Dr. Ines Kappert. The sessions on leadership and personal development by Robert Paschmann, as well as intercultural collaboration workshops facilitated by Rebeca Schröder Crespillo, contributed significantly to the program’s holistic approach.

Participants also explored themes of sustainability and innovation during a visit to the Institute for Technology Assessment and Systems Analysis (ITAS). Cultural excursions to the ZKM Center for Art and Media and Heidelberg Castle offered opportunities to connect theoretical debates with cultural and historical contexts.

We concluded the academy with a visit from Oleksandra Gnyp of Stiftung Mercator GmbH, who presented the foundation’s broader vision and encouraged us to remain engaged through the MercatorGlobe community.

I would also like to highlight the creative work produced during the program. The outcomes of this year’s Summer Academy were brought to life through the artistry and intellectual creativity of Maria Karipidou, the mind behind thinkanddraw.de. Her work captured the spirit of our collective learning experience and added a meaningful visual dimension to the program.

My sincere thanks go to Amandeep Saini-Egbers, Laura Martella, and Farisha Thakur for their continuous support throughout the academy, as well as to Stefanie Vogler-Lipp, whose efforts behind the scenes made the program possible.

The Summer Academy was an inspiring and intellectually stimulating experience. I left Karlsruhe with new perspectives, strong connections, and a renewed motivation to contribute to global dialogue and positive social change.

posts.title: Exploring the European Parliament: A Student’s Insight
posts.content:
I recently had the opportunity to visit the European Parliament and the Hemicycle in Brussels. The visit provided an instructive perspective on the institutional architecture of the European Union and offered a direct look into the environment in which legislative deliberation and democratic decision making take place. Observing the hemicycle allowed for a deeper understanding of how parliamentary processes shape the Union’s political agenda and contribute to the promotion of democracy, unity, and peace across member states.

As a student of the department of political science, engaging with one of the EU’s principal institutions was both academically enriching and professionally motivating. The experience reinforced my long-term aspiration to contribute to the work of EU bodies and to engage in initiatives aimed at advancing cooperation, governance, and constructive international dialogue.

This visit served as a meaningful reminder of the importance of supranational institutions in addressing contemporary challenges and facilitating collective action within Europe and the wider international community.

posts.title: Insights from Erasmus+ Staff Mobility in Krakow
posts.content:
I recently had the opportunity to participate in the Erasmus+ Staff Mobility for Training program at the Krakow University of Economics, held from 8 to 12 April, 2024. The program offered a dynamic and multidisciplinary learning environment that combined academic input, professional development, and cultural immersion. It brought together participants from diverse institutions and created an excellent setting for exchanging knowledge and best practices.

The training included a series of substantive sessions led by scholars and practitioners:

  • Creativity Training with Margarita Vladimyrowa
    The sessions introduced innovative approaches to problem solving and teamwork, encouraging participants to engage with creativity as a practical tool in institutional and intercultural contexts.
  • Place Branding with Sebastian Brańka, PhD
    The lecture provided a comprehensive overview of strategies for shaping the image and reputation of cities and regions. The discussion highlighted the interplay between marketing, culture, and community identity in contemporary urban development.
  • The Map of Culture and Art in Krakow with Agata Małodobry
    A guided visit to the National Museum in Krakow offered insight into the city’s artistic heritage. The tour contextualised Krakow’s cultural landscape and underscored its significance within Poland’s broader historical narrative.
  • Festivals and Cultural Programming with Professor Elżbieta Kubińska
    The session explored the spectrum of cultural festivals organised by the Krakow Festival Office, emphasising the role of artistic events in shaping public life and fostering cultural engagement.
  • Workshop on Event Management
    This practical session provided useful tools and methodologies for planning and implementing successful events, reinforcing the link between cultural programming and effective organisational practice.

Participating in this mobility program was both enriching and professionally valuable. The opportunity to engage with experts and connect with colleagues from across Europe contributed to a deeper understanding of cultural management, communication, and institutional cooperation.

I am grateful to the organisers, trainers, and fellow participants for creating an inspiring and collaborative environment. The insights gained during this week will inform and support my future work in internationalisation and cultural diplomacy.
